c.tagline: A harbor town beneath rock-cut Lycian tombs, gateway to the Blue Lagoon and the Turquoise Coast's best paragliding

card: Widely accepted at hotels, restaurants, and marina shops; small local eateries and beach vendors may prefer cash.
rides: dolmuş minibuses to Ölüdeniz and Çalış

taxi.fare: Roughly ₺30-50 flag fall plus metered per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard in town; agree a flat rate for longer trips to Ölüdeniz or Saklıkent

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Central Fethiye's marina and old town lanes are walkable, but Ölüdeniz, Kayaköy, and Saklıkent are outside town and require a dolmuş, taxi, or tour.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women; Fethiye is a well-established resort town popular with independent travelers
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the main practical caution is paragliding/adventure-sport safety rather than crime

hood_landmark.Fethiye Marina / Old Town: Fethiye Marina and the Lycian rock tombs above town
hood_landmark.Ölüdeniz: Ölüdeniz Blue Lagoon and Babadağ paragliding launch

avoid.reason: Harbor-front boat-tour touts and inflated taxi fares; keep usual awareness in the Tuesday market crowds.

hood_desc: The commercial and historic core, with the yacht marina, Tuesday market, and Lycian rock tombs carved into the cliffs above town.
A long sandy beach suburb a short dolmuş ride from central Fethiye, popular for sunset views over the bay.
The postcard Blue Lagoon beach and paragliding hub a short drive south, Turkey's most photographed stretch of coast.
A hauntingly preserved abandoned Greek village in the hills above Ölüdeniz, evacuated in the 1923 population exchange.
A hillside resort village above Ölüdeniz known for its lively bar strip and package-holiday nightlife.

water.note: Drink bottled water; tap is chlorinated but locals and visitors alike buy bottled.

transit.sys: Dolmuş (shared minibus) network connecting Fethiye to Ölüdeniz, Çalış, and outlying villages
transit.map: Dolmuş depart from the main Fethiye otogar near the marina
transit.note: Boat trips (the '12 Islands Tour') are a popular way to see the coast from Fethiye's harbor

transport.air: Dalaman Airport (DLM), about 50 km away, has direct flights from Istanbul and seasonal international routes from across Europe
transport.bus: Overnight coaches connect Fethiye to Istanbul, Izmir, and other Turkish cities via the otogar
transport.ferry: Seasonal boat tours connect Fethiye to nearby coastal towns; no scheduled international ferry
transport.car: Self-driving is popular for exploring Kayaköy, Saklıkent, and the coastal villages independently

airport.name: Dalaman Airport
airport.transport: Havaş shuttle buses and pre-booked hotel transfers; taxi transfer roughly $40-55

net.m: Good 4G/5G coverage in Fethiye and along the coast
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels and marina cafes
net.ap: A Turkcell or Vodafone tourist SIM or eSIM is recommended

tip.s: 10% is customary for tour guides, paragliding instructors, and boat crews
tip.r: 10% is standard at restaurants where service isn't already included

food.name: Fish market grill
food.desc: Buy your fish from the stalls in the covered market ring, then hand it to a surrounding restaurant which grills it and lays on salad, mezes and bread.

places.name: Fethiye Balik Pazari
places.note: The market ring itself: pick bream, calamari or prawns, agree the cooking fee first.

places.name: Oztoklu Restaurant
places.note: Family-run seafood spot inside the market, consistently rated the best of the ring.

places.name: Hilmi Restaurant
places.note: Long-established family place praised for the meze spread that comes with your fish.

food.name: Cokertme kebabi
food.desc: Mugla's own kebab: strips of beef over matchstick fried potatoes, finished with garlic yoghurt and browned butter. Named after a village up the coast.

places.name: Pasa Kebap
places.note: The town's best-known kebab house; also does a serious Adana and Iskender.

places.name: Mozaik Bahce
places.note: Garden restaurant repeatedly voted Fethiye's best; strong on regional specialities.

places.name: Carikli
places.note: Local grill house popular with residents rather than the harbour crowd.

food.name: Gozleme
food.desc: Paper-thin dough rolled by hand and griddled with cheese and parsley, spinach or spiced mince. Village women make it in front of you at the market.

places.name: Fethiye Tuesday Market
places.note: Huge weekly market with a food row of women rolling gozleme to order.

places.name: Kayakoy village eateries
places.note: The abandoned Greek village up the hill is ringed by family gozleme gardens.

places.name: Calis Beach promenade
places.note: Beachfront cafes griddle gozleme all day, good with a glass of tea.

food.name: Turkish breakfast
food.desc: Serpme kahvalti: a table covered in small plates of cheeses, olives, honey with clotted cream, tomato, eggs and jams, with endless tea. Takes two hours.

places.name: Calis Beach promenade
places.note: Row of seafront breakfast cafes with sea views and set kahvalti prices.

places.name: Kayakoy breakfast houses
places.note: Village gardens serving home preserves and village bread away from the resort strip.

places.name: Fethiye Tuesday Market
places.note: Buy cheese, olives and honey from producers, or eat at the market breakfast stalls.

food.name: Kayakoy tandir and grills
food.desc: Slow-baked lamb tandir and grill-your-own tables in the ghost village above Fethiye. You buy meat by weight and cook it over your own charcoal brazier.

places.name: Cin Bal
places.note: The famous cook-it-yourself place; pick your meat at the counter, they light the coals.

places.name: Levissi Garden
places.note: Restored old house with a garden, good for tandir and wine after walking the ruins.

food.name: Aegean meze table
food.desc: Cold plates built for slow drinking: broad beans in olive oil, sea samphire, stuffed vine leaves, octopus salad and whipped yoghurt with wild greens.

places.name: Hilmi Restaurant
places.note: The meze trolley is the reason regulars come, with the fish almost secondary.

places.name: Paspatur meyhanes
places.note: Narrow bougainvillea lanes of taverns where meze and raki run late.

places.name: Mozaik Bahce
places.note: Broad meze list in a leafy courtyard; easy for a first meze evening.

food.name: Raki
food.desc: Aniseed spirit clouded white with water, drunk slowly through a meze meal rather than as a shot. Locals call the ritual a raki sofrasi, a raki table.

places.name: Paspatur meyhanes
places.note: The traditional setting: small tables, cold meze and live fasil music some nights.

places.name: Hilmi Restaurant
places.note: Raki and grilled fish is the standard order; staff will pace the table for you.

places.name: Fethiye marina promenade
places.note: Waterfront bars for a slower raki with the yachts and the sunset.

food.name: Turkish tea and coffee
food.desc: Tulip glasses of black cay poured all day from a double kettle, and thick Turkish coffee served with a glass of water and a piece of lokum.

places.name: Paspatur tea gardens
places.note: Shaded courtyards where the tea keeps arriving until you turn the glass over.

places.name: Fethiye Tuesday Market
places.note: Tea boys weave through the stalls; the cheapest glass in town.

places.name: Fethiye marina promenade
places.note: Seafront cafes for Turkish coffee and fresh pomegranate juice by the water.

landmarks: Ölüdeniz Blue Lagoon
Turkey's most photographed beach, a sheltered turquoise lagoon curling around a white sand spit beneath pine-covered mountains.
Tomb of Amyntas and the Lycian Rock Tombs
Monumental 4th-century-BC temple facades carved into the cliffs above town, glowing honey-gold at sunset over Fethiye's rooftops.
Kayaköy Ghost Village
A haunting hillside of 350-plus roofless stone houses abandoned in the 1923 Greek-Turkish population exchange, now an open-air museum.
Butterfly Valley
A dramatic boat-access canyon where a waterfall-fed beach and rare Jersey tiger butterflies hide between 350-meter cliffs.
Saklıkent Gorge
One of Europe's deepest canyons, an 18-kilometer marble crack where visitors wade through icy waters between walls 300 meters high.
Babadağ Mountain
The 1,969-meter paragliding mecca above Ölüdeniz, its cable car whisking non-flyers to sunset terraces with staggering coastal views.
Fethiye Fish Market (Balık Pazarı)
A lively market square where you buy the catch of the day and surrounding restaurants grill it at your table for a small fee.
Telmessos Amphitheatre
A partly restored Hellenistic-Roman theatre facing the harbor, the most visible remnant of the ancient Lycian city beneath modern Fethiye.
Çalış Beach
A four-kilometer pebble-and-sand strand famed for flaming sunsets over the Twelve Islands, backed by a relaxed promenade of bars and cafes.
Tlos Ruins
One of Lycia's oldest cities, a day-trip-worthy acropolis stacking rock tombs, a Roman theatre and an Ottoman fortress beneath the Taurus peaks.

train.note: There is no railway anywhere on the Turquoise Coast, so no trains serve Fethiye. The nearest station is at Denizli, roughly 4 hours inland by road, from where regional trains run to İzmir. Most visitors arrive by coach or fly into Dalaman airport, about an hour away.

bus.note: No international coaches. Fethiye's otogar has regular services to Antalya (about 4 hours on the coast road, 3 inland), Marmaris, Denizli for Pamukkale, İzmir and overnight coaches to Istanbul, run by Pamukkale (https://www.pamukkale.com.tr/) and Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/). Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/). Dolmuş minibuses cover Ölüdeniz, Kayaköy and Çalış.

ferry.note: The Rhodes catamaran sails from Fethiye harbour a few days a week in the summer season only and takes about 90 minutes - bring your passport and note that Greek entry rules apply. Nothing runs in winter. Fethiye is also the classic starting point for the multi-day gulet 'blue cruise' down the coast to Olympos, which is a chartered tour rather than scheduled transport.

half.name: Dalyan & Kaunos Rock Tombs
half.blurb: Riverside town with Lycian rock-cut tombs carved into cliffs above the Dalyan River and nearby İztuzu turtle beach.

half.name: Xanthos & Patara Ancient Ruins
half.blurb: Former Lycian capital's ruins paired with Patara's colonnaded street and Turkey's longest undeveloped sand beach.

half.name: Rhodes
half.blurb: Greek island reachable by fast ferry in under two hours, its medieval Old Town a UNESCO World Heritage site.

full.name: Pamukkale & Hierapolis
full.blurb: Blindingly white travertine terraces of mineral pools beside the Roman ruins of ancient Hierapolis, about four hours away.
